output.summary: An evergreen tree native to South America. It has a rounded crown of slender, willow-like drooping branches, while its bark contains strongly fragrant resin and rubbed leaves smell of turpentine. Its aromatic red fruits taste sweet and spicy and are eaten as a pepper substitute.
output.edibilityNote: Fruits are eaten as a pepper substitute; a 16th-century account says ancient Peruvians made alcoholic drink, vinegar and a honey-like product from them.
